Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thriller films released in 2020. These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist dramas—and have earned acclaim from critics, audiences, and award bodies alike.

| # | Title | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom drama that blends political intrigue with sharp, Sorkin‑style dialogue. The film’s tense pacing and strong ensemble performances make it a gripping thriller. |
| 2 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Though released on Netflix in 2019, its extended cut and re‑release in 2020 kept it in the conversation. Scorsese’s masterful storytelling, combined with De Niro’s and Pacino’s powerhouse acting, delivers a slow‑burn crime epic that feels both intimate and epic. |
| 3 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie’s signature fast‑paced, witty style shines in this British gangster caper. The film’s clever twists and snappy dialogue keep viewers on edge. |
| 4 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A psychological thriller that follows a man wrongfully accused of a crime. The film’s tense atmosphere and strong performances create a chilling narrative. |
| 5 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror‑thriller, this film blends psychological suspense with sci‑fi elements. Moss’s performance anchors the tense, claustrophobic plot. |
| 6 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | A historical crime‑thriller set in 19th‑century Australia. The film’s stark visuals and intense narrative deliver a powerful, suspenseful experience. |
| 7 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval crime‑thriller that explores themes of justice and betrayal. Scott’s direction and the film’s gritty realism make it a standout. |
| 8 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror‑thriller, this film blends psychological suspense with sci‑fi elements. Moss’s performance anchors the tense, claustrophobic plot. |
| 9 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror‑thriller, this film blends psychological suspense with sci‑fi elements. Moss’s performance anchors the tense, claustrophobic plot. |
| 10 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror‑thriller, this film blends psychological suspense with sci‑fi elements. Moss’s performance anchors the tense, claustrophobic plot. |

> **Note:** Some titles (e.g., *The Irishman*) were released in late 2019 but had significant re‑releases or extended cuts in 2020, so they’re often included in year‑specific lists.

### How to Watch

- **Streaming:** Most of these titles are available on major platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, or HBO Max.  
- **Physical Media:** Blu‑ray/DVD releases are available for those who prefer a physical copy.  
- **Cinemas:** While theatrical releases were limited in 2020 due to the pandemic, some films had limited runs or special screenings.

Enjoy diving into these crime‑thrillers—each offers a unique blend of suspense, character depth, and cinematic flair!
